rationale: 17 of 18 checklist items are satisfied, including every item that speaks directly to the phase's central mission: false credit via structural proximity or numeric coincidence is mechanically prevented, all 14 previously-known false credits are independently caught, the adversarial suite is comprehensive and passing, cross-dataset generalization required zero package-specific tuning, ground-truth integrity was preserved, and production code was verifiably untouched. However, criterion H - the evaluator's own agreement with a genuinely independent, blinded second-pass reviewer - was NOT satisfied under either of the pre-registered thresholds, and the disagreement rate (especially on detailed disposition class, 37.3% vs a required 85%) is too large to describe as a rounding error. Per the phase's own explicit instruction ('If thresholds are missed: investigate evaluator ambiguity. Do not rewrite disagreements after seeing them'), this was investigated (not patched), and the investigation found a real, identifiable, and very plausibly correctable cause (a definitional communication gap about what 'representation' requires, compounded by the fact that no live semantic AI judge was ever run at all in this phase, so the evaluator's own most nuanced layer was never truly exercised). This is a genuine methodology-validity gap, not evidence that the central false-credit defect has returned - but a validation gate is a validation gate, and this phase is explicitly 'primarily a methodology-validity gate.' Declaring an unqualified PASS while a required independent-validation threshold was missed by this margin would repeat exactly the kind of rounding-up this whole phase exists to prevent.

prohibitedClaimsCheck.statement: None of the prohibited claims (phase charter Section 35) appear anywhere in this artifact set or the accompanying report.

whatThisVerdictDoesNotMean: A PASS on the OTHER 17 criteria does not mean the underlying product's semantic coverage is good - quite the opposite: the DSGR aggregate metrics (07-dsgr-v2-aggregate-metrics.json) show combined CRITICAL+MATERIAL semantic recall of roughly 5/803 (0.6%) and 175 dangerous-unaccounted CRITICAL/MATERIAL units under V2's own honest, non-inflated accounting - dramatically lower than any historical percentage this codebase has published. Per the phase charter's own Section 33, this is treated as a SUCCESS of the evaluator (it is telling the truth instead of granting false credit), not a reason to fail the evaluator - and it is emphatically not evidence that Phase 3F.2 or Phase 4 readiness has improved; if anything it is the opposite.
